description: Handler mode: a CONNECT to /mcp passes the target-form, path, state and body checks, but CONNECT (like TRACE and TRACK) is a forbidden method no web Request can carry, so it is answered 400 {"error":"request cannot be represented as a web Request"} without calling the handler, the same byte-exact reply as target_unrepresentable_400, never a 405 or a 500. MCPWARP.md §4.5
in:
CONNECT /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: notes-tester.mcpwarp.test
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
out:
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 58

{"error":"request cannot be represented as a web Request"}
notes: The fetch standard's forbidden methods (CONNECT, TRACE, TRACK, matched case-insensitively) make the Request constructor throw; an SDK whose request type could carry them still answers this 400 in both modes, so the runtimes agree. The target is origin-form /mcp so that only the method decides; a CONNECT with an authority-form target is the earlier 400 unsupported request target form.
